PR Summary by Qodo

Expose raw delivery data in public score snapshots ✨ Enhancement 🧪 Tests 📝 Documentation 🕐 20-40 Minutes
AI Description

>
>• Exposes original BallEvent payloads in score snapshots for on-call debugging.
>• Extends the public schema and tests to guarantee raw delivery serialization.
>• Appends an unexplained testing marker to the README.
>
Diagram

```mermaid graph TD A["BallEvent"] --> B["Scoring engine"] --> C["ScoreSnapshot"] --> D["Score API"] --> E["Broadcast clients"] A -. "raw copy" .-> C D --> F["Support tooling"] ```
High-Level Assessment

>The following are alternative approaches to this PR:
1. Authenticated debug endpoint
- ➕ Preserves ScoreSnapshot as a scoring-owned public contract - ➕ Restricts raw protocol fields to authorized support users - ➕ Allows independent retention and redaction policies - ➖ Adds endpoint authorization and maintenance - ➖ Requires support tooling to make a separate request
2. Correlated structured event logs
- ➕ Keeps raw events outside product-facing responses - ➕ Supports historical incident investigation - ➕ Avoids downstream compile-time or behavioral coupling - ➖ Requires searchable log infrastructure and retention - ➖ Needs correlation identifiers and operational tooling
>**Recommendation:** Use a restricted debug endpoint or correlated structured logs instead of adding raw_ball to ScoreSnapshot. The current approach is simple, but a documentation warning cannot prevent broadcast clients from depending on extras.type or umpire_confirmed and bypassing the engine’s scoring-owned interpretation.

apply_ball copies the complete BallEvent into ScoreSnapshot.raw_ball, contradicting the
scoring-owned public contract and exposing inputs such as extras.type and
wicket.umpire_confirmed alongside interpreted results. Both response-model endpoints serialize
this field, so an unconfirmed LBW reaches clients as both last_event.wicket_counted == false and
raw wicket data that lets downstream tooling skip the engine's decision.
